commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark command for task completion
commitResults.messageBody: Track each task's completion state alongside its description so the existing in-memory task list can mark a selected task as done without introducing another class. Show task status in the list and confirm successful mark operations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add unmark command for task completion
commitResults.messageBody: Allow users to reverse a task's done status using its list number. This mirrors the mark command, preserves validation for invalid task numbers, and gives a clear confirmation of the updated state.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task state into Task class
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce a dedicated Task type that owns a task's description and completion state. Quackers now stores Task objects and delegates marking, unmarking, and display formatting to them, eliminating the parallel arrays used by the earlier commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save task list between application runs
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks exist only in memory and disappear when Quackers exits.

Persist task types, details, and completion status in a text file.

Save after each change and create the data directory when needed.

Isolate UI tests so saved data cannot leak between test cases.

Deadline dates are unrestricted text and cannot be validated.

Accept ISO dates and display them in a friendlier English format.

Keep persisted dates in ISO format so reloads remain stable.

Add UI coverage for valid, malformed, and impossible dates.

Quackers handles parsing, storage, list operations, and console IO.

Separate those responsibilities into Parser, TaskList, Storage, and Ui.

Keep Quackers focused on coordinating commands and preserve behavior.

Application classes live in the default package.

Move them into the quackers package under the Java source root.

Update development instructions and UI tests for the package path.

The project relies on IDE or manual Java compilation.

Integrate the supplied Gradle wrapper and Java 25 build configuration.

Point Gradle at the packaged Quackers entry point and archive name.

Increase wrapper download resilience without weakening TLS checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for parsing and storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Command parsing and file persistence contain core branching logic.

Test valid and invalid parsing, missing files, and corrupt records.

Verify mixed task data and completion state survive a save/load cycle.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use descriptive names for task details
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and event fields use short prepositions as names. Those names
have class-wide scope and do not reveal what their values represent.

Rename the fields and accessors to identify the date and times explicitly.
Also give the storage exception factory a verb-led name, as required for
methods.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to find matching tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Search task descriptions without regard to case so users can locate related tasks while preserving their original order. Validate missing keywords and cover the command with unit and console UI tests.

Javadoc parameter descriptions omit their closing punctuation. This makes
the public API comments inconsistent with the required Javadoc form.

Add periods to every parameter description in production code so the API
documentation follows the course coding standard.
Integrate persistent task storage while preserving the completed increment branch.
Integrate typed deadline dates after the persistence increment.
Integrate the separation of parsing, storage, task-list, and UI responsibilities.
Integrate the package structure required for the application classes.
Integrate the Gradle build before the test and JAR increments.
Integrate automated parser and storage tests into the Gradle build.
Integrate descriptive naming and Javadoc convention fixes before adding the find command.
Integrate task-description search while retaining the coding-standard corrections.

A GUI needs the reply to a command as a String, but Ui printed every message
straight to System.out, so the only way to obtain a reply was to capture stdout.

Change Ui's message methods to return their text instead of printing it, and add
Ui#show to do the console printing (indenting each line, as before). Quackers now
exposes getResponse(String), which executes one command and returns the reply;
run() uses it for the console loop, and the upcoming GUI will use it too.

Command errors are no longer thrown out of getResponse: both front ends want to
display the problem and carry on, so it returns the error text as the reply.

Console output is unchanged, so the existing text UI test plan still applies.

Quackers now runs as a chat-style window instead of only in a terminal.

build.gradle follows the sample given in the se-education JavaFX tutorial: the
javafx-base/controls/fxml/graphics artifacts at 17.0.7, with the win, mac and
linux classifiers all listed so the project builds on any machine. mainClass
becomes quackers.Launcher, because a main class that extends Application makes
the JVM demand a modular JavaFX runtime that we do not have on the classpath.

The layout is defined in FXML rather than hand-built in Java, so it can be
tweaked in Scene Builder without touching code, and the view stays separate from
the controller:

- MainWindow.fxml / MainWindow  - the window and its input handling
- DialogBox.fxml / DialogBox    - one chat bubble; uses the fx:root construct so
                                  each instance is its own root and controller

MainWindow calls the Quackers#getResponse added earlier, so no task logic is
duplicated in the GUI. bye is kept as a command, per the requirements: it now
disables the input and closes the window after a short pause, so the farewell
stays readable.

The console UI is retained; Quackers#main still runs it, which keeps the text UI
test plan usable for checking the core logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document how to run the GUI and the console UI
commitResults.messageBody:
The setup steps still pointed at Quackers.main() and showed the old Duke banner
as the expected output, which no longer matches what a new user sees. Point them
at Launcher.main() instead, and add a short section covering both interfaces,
building the JAR, and where task data is saved.
